step.title: Put something you cook on the menu
step.body: Your restaurant is empty right now, and nothing else in here works until something is on the menu. Pick one dish you sell every day - the rest of this walkthrough is built around it.

step.title: Open Catalog
step.body: In the main menu. Everything you put on a menu lives behind this one item.

step.title: Go to Products
step.body: The products card on this page.

step.title: Add your first product
step.body: New Product, at the top right.

step.title: A name, a price, a category
step.body: That is all a cooked dish needs to exist. What it is made of is a separate question and we answer it shortly, with a recipe - so put in the dish itself and save it. Real food, real price: everything you do from here counts.

step.title: You have a menu
step.body: One dish, and the till can already sell it. Next: the stock you sell exactly as it arrives.

mission.title: Stock you sell as it comes

step.title: A bottle of water is not cooked
step.body: Some of what you sell is bought and sold unchanged - a soft drink, a packet of crisps, a bottle of water. That is stock rather than a dish, and one tick puts it on the till beside your food.

step.title: Open Inventory
step.body: Items, suppliers, recipes, purchase orders and consumption all sit behind this one.

step.title: Go to Inventory Items
step.body: Every physical thing you buy is counted here, whether you cook with it or sell it.

step.title: Add a new item
step.body: New Item, at the top right. Something you sell exactly as you buy it.

step.title: Tick Directly Sellable
step.body: That tick is the whole difference. It gives the item a selling price and puts it on the till beside your dishes, and selling one takes it straight off this outlet’s shelf - no recipe, because nothing is made. Fill the rest in and save.

step.title: That one is on the counter now
step.body: Bought and sold as one thing, counted as one thing. Next: the stock nobody ever buys on its own.

step.title: Now the things nobody orders
step.body: Chicken, flour, cheese - stock that only ever leaves the building inside a dish. Add two of them now and leave them unsellable; the next mission joins them to the dish you made first.

step.title: Add the first ingredient
step.body: Same button, same form. Buy it in the unit it actually arrives in - a sack, a carton, a kilo.

step.title: Leave this one unticked
step.body: Unticked means it never appears on the till - nobody walks in and buys a kilo of your flour. It moves only when a dish that needs it is sold, and the recipe is what tells the system how much.

step.title: Now a second one
step.body: One more ingredient the same way. Two is enough to make the recipe worth reading.

step.title: Two ingredients on the books
step.body: Counted, but not connected to anything yet. That is the next mission, and it is the one that makes stock look after itself.

step.title: Tell it what the dish is made of
step.body: A recipe is the link between the dish from mission one and the two ingredients you have just added. Once it exists, selling the dish takes its ingredients off the shelf without anybody writing anything down - which is the whole reason to keep stock in here at all.

step.title: Back to Inventory
step.body: In the main menu.

step.title: Go to Recipes
step.body: The recipes card on this page.

step.title: Choose the dish you made
step.body: Pick it from the list. A recipe belongs to a dish, so everything below now applies to that one and nothing else.

step.title: One line per ingredient
step.body: Add a row for each of your two and say how much one portion uses. The unit shown is the one you bought it in, so a quarter of a kilo is 0.25 - nothing to convert in your head.

step.title: Save the recipe
step.body: Save Recipe, under the table.

step.title: The dish knows its own ingredients
step.body: From now on, selling it moves exactly these quantities and nothing else. Next: the things a recipe cannot measure.

step.title: Some things you cannot measure per plate
step.body: Nobody weighs the frying oil for one portion of chicken. Oil, sauce, gas, cleaning supplies - not sold on their own, not worth putting in a recipe, and still money. They get counted a third way, and this mission adds one.

step.title: Add one of those
step.body: Cooking oil, a sauce, whatever your kitchen goes through without counting.

step.title: Bought in drums, used by the day
step.body: Fill it in like an ingredient and leave Directly Sellable unticked. Buy it in the unit the delivery note uses - a drum, a five-litre bottle - because that is the number you will be checking against.

step.title: That one moves by hand
step.body: Nothing will ever deduct it for you - no till, no recipe. You tell the system when it goes, and there is a mission near the end for exactly that. First, let us buy all four.

mission.title: Buy all four in one order

step.title: Nothing is on the shelf yet
step.body: Four items exist and every one of them is at zero, because creating an item is not the same as buying it. Stock arrives through a purchase order: one form that tells the supplier what you want, puts the delivery on the shelf, and writes the cost into your accounts.

step.title: Open Inventory
step.body: In the main menu.

step.title: Go to Purchase Orders
step.body: The purchase orders card on this page.

step.title: Start a new order
step.body: Create PO, at the top right.

step.title: Who you are buying from
step.body: Pick a supplier - and if the list is empty, add one under Inventory first, then come back. Every order you place against a supplier builds a history you can hold them to.

step.title: All four items, one line each
step.body: Add a line for each one you created - the sellable one, both ingredients and the oil - with the quantity and what you actually paid. The total adds itself up as you type, and that unit price becomes the item’s cost.

step.title: Received means it is on the shelf
step.body: Leave it on Received and saving puts every one of these quantities into the outlet’s stock. Pending or Approved records the order without moving anything - for stock still on its way.

step.title: Save the order
step.body: Create PO, at the bottom of the form.

step.title: Four items, all in stock
step.body: Ordered, delivered, counted and costed from one form, without writing it down twice. Now let us see what that did to the storeroom.

mission.title: What is on the shelf now

step.title: The screen that stops you running out
step.body: Running out mid-service costs you the table and the reputation. This one screen answers what you have, what it is worth, and what to reorder - and you have just given it something real to say.

step.title: Open Reporting
step.body: In the main menu.

step.title: Click Inventory Health
step.body: In the row of tabs. This one ignores the date filter on purpose - stock is what you have now, not what you had.

step.title: What needs reordering
step.body: Anything at or under the minimum stock level you set on the item itself. Set that level on each of your four and this number starts doing the ordering for you.

step.title: Money sitting on the shelves
step.body: What you paid on the purchase order, still unsold. Stock is cash you have already spent, and this is how much of it is waiting.

step.title: Your four items, in one list
step.body: Low stock first, always, so the trouble is at the top. Take a note of what each of your four says right now - the next two missions are about changing these very numbers.

step.title: The storeroom, without walking to it
step.body: That is stock coming in. Next: stock going out, at the till.

step.title: Take one sale with your own menu
step.body: Sell your dish and your sellable item in the same order, then come back to that list. Both come off the shelf - and they come off in completely different ways, which is the point of this mission.

step.title: Open the POS
step.body: This is the screen your counter staff will live on all day.

step.title: Tap your dish, then your item
step.body: They sit side by side here - the one you cook and the one that came straight off the delivery - because to somebody at the counter there is no difference. One tap each.

step.title: The bill builds itself
step.body: Quantities, a note for the kitchen, a discount on one line or on the lot - with the tax and the total recalculated as you go.

step.title: Place the order
step.body: It goes to the kitchen screen and the orders board in the same instant. This is a real order in your restaurant.

step.title: Both fell, for different reasons
step.body: The sellable item came off one for one, because you sold the thing itself. The dish never moved - what moved is the two ingredients, by the exact amounts in your recipe. The oil has not moved at all, and that is correct.

step.title: Selling now keeps its own count
step.body: Two of the three ways stock moves, both automatic. The third one is the oil, and it is the only one that needs you.

step.title: Stock leaves without a sale
step.body: Oil gets used, staff eat, things spill and things get thrown away. None of it goes through the till, so none of it comes off by itself - you report it, and the shelf drops the moment you do.

step.title: Open Inventory
step.body: In the main menu.

step.title: Go to Report Consumption
step.body: The last card on this page.

step.title: Log some consumption
step.body: Log Consumption, at the top right.

step.title: Outlet, date, item, quantity
step.body: Pick the oil you added, say how much went and why. Saving deducts it from that outlet straight away - and deleting the log later puts it back, so a mistake costs you nothing.

step.title: Every entry, with a name on it
step.body: Who reported what, when, and whether it was corrected afterwards. This is the difference between stock that was used and stock that is simply missing.

step.title: And the shelf agrees
step.body: The oil has dropped by exactly what you reported. That is the last of the four moving, and every one of them now has a reason for every unit it loses.

step.title: Your restaurant is set up
step.body: A dish, a recipe, stock you sell as it comes, stock you use by hand, a delivery in and a sale out. One last thing worth knowing before you carry on alone.

step.title: You can always start this again
step.body: Close it whenever you like and go and set the rest up yourself - it keeps your place. Here is where it lives, so you can find it again, or hand it to whoever does your stock.

step.title: Open My Profile
step.body: Right at the bottom of the main menu.

step.title: This card, on your profile
step.body: It remembers where you got to - against you, not against this browser. Close it on your phone and pick it up on a laptop at the same step.

step.title: Continue, or start over
step.body: Continue picks up at the step you left. Start over goes back to the first mission - useful when you are showing a new manager how the stock works.

step.title: You know how the whole thing works now
step.body: Menu, stock, recipes, buying, selling and what leaves without being sold - and you did every one of them yourself, with your own food. The walkthrough is on your profile whenever you want it back, and there is one last thing worth saying before you go.

step.title: It is all yours to keep
step.body: Your dish, your recipe, your stock and your first sale are already in here - subscribing changes nothing on these screens except the date they stop working. The introductory price is on right now, and there is no set-up cost on top of it: nothing to pay to be installed, configured or trained. If you would rather ask a person first, we are on WhatsApp and we answer.
